6100.full: a plant used for stuffing or padding; and metaphorically " padding , " an expletive , (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

s: The material elements of the universe
6101.full: στοιχεῖον, -ου, τό [in LXX: Wis.7:17 19:18, 4Ma.12:13 * ;] prop., one of a row (στοῖχος) or series, hence, __1. the shadow-line of a dial (Aristoph.). __2. an elementary sound or letter of the alphabet (Anth., Plut., π.). __3. the elements or rudiments of knowledge (Arist., al.) Heb.5:12; πτωχὰ σ., Gal.4:9; σ. τοῦ κόσμου, Gal.4:3, Col.2:8, 20 (but see infr.). __4. The material elements of the universe (Plat.; LXX, ll. with): 2Pe.3:10 3:12. __5. The heavenly bodies (Ding. Laert.). __6. The demons or tutelary spirits of nature (Enoch., Test., Sol., al.; for this sense in Ga, Col, ll. with, see ICC on Col.2:8; Enc. Bibl., see word " Elements ").† (AS)

6104.full: στρατεία (on the orthogr., see Deiss., BS, 181 f.), -ας, ἡ (οτρατεύω), [in LXX chiefly for צָבָא ;] an expedition, a campaign, warfare: metaphorically, 2Co.10:4 (-τιά, T), 1Ti.1:18.† (AS)

6105.full: 1. the office, dignity , or post of general, command , (Herdotus Historicus), attic; of naval command, (Xenophon Historicus) 2. the office of στρατηγός at Athens, a sort of war-minister , (Aristophanes Comicus):—;at Rome the Praetorship , (Plutarch) 3. a period of command, campaign , (Xenophon Historicus) 4. the qualities or skill of a general, generalship , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

6106.full: twisted, crooked , (Aristotle Philosopher); of the brows, knit, wrinkled , [variant datesAnthology Palantina: metaphorically, στρεβλοῖσι παλαίσμασι by cunning dodges in wrestling, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

6107.full: the socket in which the pivot of a door ὁ στρόφιγξ); moved, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

s: to have a sombre, gloomy appearance
6109.full: στυγνάζω (στυγνός, sombre, gloomy, sullen, Isa.5:17, Wis.17:5, Dan LXX 2:12*), [in LXX: Eze.27:35 28:19 32:10 (שָׁמֵם)* ;] to have a sombre, gloomy appearance: of the human countenance (RV, his countenance fell), Mrk.10:22; of the sky (so στυγνότης, Polyb., iv, 21, 1), Mat.16:3 ([WH], R, mg., om.).† (AS)

6110.full: 1. hated, abhorred, hateful , (Aeschulus Tragicus):—;with dative hateful or hostile to one, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 2. gloomy, sullen , Lat. tristis, (Aeschulus Tragicus); ὁρᾶν στυγνός gloomy to behold, (Xenophon Historicus);—; στυγνὸς εἴκων yielding sullenly, with an ill grace , (Sophocles Tragicus); neuter as adverb, (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

6111.lxx: in LXX: Exo.14:13 A, Jdg.16:26 B, 3Ki.8:11 B *
6111.full: στήκω late Pres., formed from perf., ἕστηκα (see B1., § 17; WH, App., 169; Kennedy, Sources, 158; M, Pr., 238; MM, xxiii), [in LXX: Exo.14:13 A, Jdg.16:26 B, 3Ki.8:11 B * ;] = ἵστημι, to stand: Mrk.3:31 11:25, Jhn.1:26, Rev.12:4 (ἕστηκεν T). Metaphorical, to stand firm, stand fast: absol., Gal.5:1 (but see Field, Notes, 189 f.), 2Th.2:15; before ἐν, Jhn.8:44 (ἕστηκεν, T, R, mg.), 1Co.16:13, Php.1:27 4:1; with dative, Rom.14:4.† (AS)

6114.full: συν-γνώμη (Rec. συγγ-), -ης, ἡ (συγγιγνώσκω, (a) to agree with; (b) to pardon), [in LXX: Sir prol.14 (B1N1 cm.) 313, 2Mac 14:20* ;] __1. confession. __2. fellow feeling; hence, concession, allowance: 1Co.7:6 (see ICC, in l). __3. pardon.† (AS)

6115.full: 1. to strike together; ς. τὼ χεῖρε to clap the hands for joy, (Xenophon Historicus); but also to smite them together in grief, (Lucian):—;Pass. to be applauded , (Xenophon Historicus) 2. to hammer or weld together , (Aristophanes Comicus): hence, to weld a number of men into one body, i. e. organise them, (Demosthenes Orator), etc.:—;perfect passive participle συγκεκροτημένος well-trained, in good discipline , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

6117.full: συν-χαίρω (Rec. συγ-), [in LXX: Gen.21:6 (צָחַק), 3Ma.1:8 R * ;] __1. to rejoice with: with dative of person(s), Luk.1:58 15:6, 9, Php.2:17-18, EV; with dative of thing(s), 1Co.12:26 13:6. __2. to congratulate (Æschin., Polyb., al.): Phi, l.with (Lft., in I.; cf. MM, xxiv).† (AS)

6118.full: συν-ζεύγνυμι (Rec. συζ-), [in LXX: Eze.1:11, 23 (חָבַר) * ;] to yoke to­gether: metaphorically, of union in wedlock, Mat.19:6, Mrk.10:9.† (AS)

s: one who informed against persons exporting figs
one who brings figs to light by shaking the tree
one who makes rich men yield up their fruit by false accusations)
6120.full: a false accuser, slanderer , (Aristophanes Comicus), etc.; (never used in the modern sense of sycophant , i. e. κόλαξ); generally, a false adviser , (Demosthenes Orator) (Commonly derived from σῦκον, φαίνω, one who informed against persons exporting figs from Attica: better perhaps a fig-shewer , i. e. one who brings figs to light by shaking the tree (the figs having been hidden in the thick foliage); and then, metaphorically, one who makes rich men yield up their fruit by false accusations). (ML)

6121.full: 1. computation , (Plato Philosophus) 2. a conclusion, inference from premisses , (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

s: to be moved to grief by sympathy
6122.full: συν-λυπέω (Rec. συλλ-), -ῶ, [in LXX: Psa.69:20, Isa.51:19 (נוּד) * ;] to make to grieve with (Arist.). Pass., to be moved to grief by sympathy: before ἐπί, with dative, Mrk.3:5.† (AS)

6124.full: συμπαθής, -ές (σύν, πάσχω) [in LXX: Job.29:25 A (אָבֵל), 4Ma.5:25 א, 4Ma.13:23 4Mac 15:4 * ;] __1. affected by like feelings, sympathetic: 1Pe.3:8. __2. exciting sympathy (Jb, l.with; Dion. H.).† (AS)

6126.full: to join in war , (Thucydides), etc.; τινί with one, (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

6127.full: to join in escorting , (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; ς. τινὰ ναυσίν (Thucydides) (ML)

6129.lxx: in LXX: Tob.12:12 ΑΒ, Pro.8:27 (?), Wis.9:10 *
6129.full: συν-πάρειμι (Rec. σνμπ-), [in LXX: Tob.12:12 ΑΒ, Pro.8:27 (?), Wis.9:10 * ;] to be present together or with: with dative of person(s), Act.25:24.† (AS)

6131.lxx: in LXX: Dan LXX TH Dan.3:5, 15,  TH Dan.3:7, 10 (סוּמְפּוֹנְיָה) 4Ma.14:3 A *
6131.full: συμφωνία, -ας, ἡ (σύμφωνος), [in LXX: Dan LXX TH Dan.3:5, 15, TH Dan.3:7, 10 (סוּמְפּוֹנְיָה) 4Ma.14:3 A * ;] __1. symphony, music: Luk.15:25 __2. a musical instrument (Polyb., al.; Da, ll. with; v MM, xxiv).† (AS)

6132.full: συν-ακολουθέω, -ῶ [in LXX: 2Ma.2:4 2Mac 2:6 * ;] to follow along with, accompany: with dative of person(s), Mrk.14:51, Luk.23:49; before μετά, with genitive of person(s), Mrk.5:37.† (AS)

6133.full: συν-αυξάνω [in LXX: 2Ma.4:4, 4Ma.13:27 * ;] to cause to increase or grow together. Pass., to grow together: Mat.13:30 (Xen., al.).† (AS)

s: the members of a picnic party
6134.full: to dine or sup with another, with dative, (Xenophon Historicus); μετά τινων (Demosthenes Orator):—;absolute to dine or sup with others , (Xenophon Historicus), etc.; οἱ ξυνδειπνοῦντες the members of a picnic party , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

6136.full: συνδρομή, -ῆς, ἡ (συντρέχω), [in LXX: Jdth.10:18, 3Ma.3:8 * ;] concourse, esp. of a riotous gathering: Act.21:30 (Arist., Polyb., al.).† (AS)

6137.lxx: in LXX: Exo.23:5 B2 (עָזַב), Isa.14:9 (עוּר pil.), 4Ma.2:14 *
6137.full: συν-εγείρω [in LXX: Exo.23:5 B2 (עָזַב), Isa.14:9 (עוּר pil.), 4Ma.2:14 * ;] to raise together: metaphorically, of the Christian's mystical resur­rection with Christ, Eph.2:6; pass., Col.2:12 3:1.† (AS)

6139.full: συν-ελαύνω [in LXX: 2Ma.4:26 2Mac 4:42 2Mac 5:5 * ;] to drive together, force together: εἰς εἰρήνην, Act.7:26, Rec. (WH, RV, συνήλλασσεν).† (AS)

6143.full: συνεργέω, -ῶ [in LXX: I Est.7:2, 1Ma.12:1 * ;] __1. prop., to work together (with): absol., Mrk.16:20, 1Co.16:16, 2Co.6:1; with dative, Jas.2:22; dative commod., Rom.8:28, T, R, txt. (but see infr.). __2. In Hellenistic writers (M, Pr., 65), trans., to cause to work together (cf. ICC, in l): with accusative of thing(s), Rom.8:28 [WH] R, mg. (but see supr.).† (AS)

6144.full: συνεργός, -όν [in LXX: 2Ma.8:7 Mac 14:5 * ;] a fellow-worker: with genitive of person(s), Rom.16:3, 9 16:21, Php.2:25 4:3, 1Th.3:2, Rec., Phm 1 24; θεοῦ (cf. Lft., Notes, 41, 188), 1Co.3:9 (pl.), 1Th.3:2 [WH] R, mg. (R, txt., διάκονον τοῦ θ.; on the original reading, see ICC, in l); τ. χαρᾶς ὑηῶν, 2Co.1:24; τ. ἀληθείᾳ, III Jn 8; before εἰς, 2Co.8:23, Col.4:11.† (AS)

6146.full: συν-είδησις, -εως, ἡ (συνεῖδον), [in LXX: Ecc.10:20 (מַדָּע), Wis.17:11, Sir.42:18 א * ;] __1. consciousness: with genitive obj., Heb.10:2, 1Pe.2:19. __2. In ethical sense, innate discernment, self-judging consciousness, conscience (Stoics and late writers): Rom.2:15 9:1, 1Co.10:29, 2Co.1:12 4:2 5:11, 1Ti.4:2, Heb.9:14; σ. ἀγαθή, Act.23:1, 1Ti.1:5 1:19, 1Pe.3:16 3:21; ἀσθενής, 1Co.8:7 8:10; ἀσθενοῦσα, 1Co.8:12; ἀπρόσκοπος, Act.24:16; καθαρά, 1Ti.3:9, 2Ti.1:3; καλή, Heb.13:18; πονηρά, Heb.10:22; ὁ νοῦς καὶ ἡ σ., Tit.1:15; διὰ τὴν σ., Rom.13:5, 1Co.10:25 10:27-28; κατὰ σ., Heb.9:9; ὑπὸ (τῆς) σ., Jhn.8:1-59 [9] (Rec.), 1Co.10:29 (cf. Cremer, 233 ff.; ICC on Rom.2:15; DB, i, 468 ff.).† (AS)

6149.full: a mutual agreement, covenant, contract , (Demosthenes Orator), etc.: in plural dealings between men , (Aristotle Philosopher) (ML)

6150.full: to sew or stitch together, sew up , Lat. consuo, (Hesiod) (ML)

to move like a swing, to swing to and fro
6154.full: 1. to sling, to use the sling , (Thucydides) 2. to strike by slinging , (Babrius Fabularum Scriptor) 3. to throw as from a sling :—;Pass., (Euripides) 4. to move like a swing, to swing to and fro , (Euripides) from σφενδόνη (ML)

6156.full: σφυρόν, -οῦ, τό, [in LXX: Job.41:21 (לָהַט) * ;] the ankle: Act.3:7, Rec. (T, WH, σφυδρόν; see Bl., § 6, 8).† (AS)

6157.full: a wedge , (Aristophanes Comicus), etc.;—;used as an instrument of torture , (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

6158.full: 1. a vertebra , (Aristophanes Comicus):—;in plural the backbone, spine , or the neck , (Euripides) 2. Lat. verticillus, the round weight attached to a spindle, (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

s: of or for the body, bodily
6160.full: σωματικός, -ή, -όν (σῶμα), [in LXX: 4Ma.1:32 4Mac 3:1 * ;] __(a) of or for the body, bodily: γυμνασία, 1Ti.4:8; __(b) (opposite to ἀσώματος) bodily, corporeal: εἶδος, Luk.3:22.† (AS)

6161.full: σωρεύω [in LXX: Pro.25:22 (חָתָה), Jdth.15:11 * ;] __(a) to heap on: with accusative before ἐπί with accusative, Rom.12:20 (LXX) (Arist., al.); __(b) to heap with: with accusative and dative, metaphorically, ἁμαρτίαις, 2Ti.3:6 (overwhelmed with, Field, Notes, 217) (Polyb.).† (AS)

6164.full: σάτον, -ου, τό (Aram. סָאתָא = Heb. סְאָה), [in LXX: Hag.2:17 (16)* ;] a Hebrew measure (= about a peck and a half): Mat.13:33, Luk.13:21.† (AS)

6165.full: 1. Pass. to lie together , (Sophocles Tragicus) 2. as Pass. of συντίθημι, to be composed or compounded , ἔκ τινων of certain parts, (Plato Philosophus), etc. 3. of written works, to be composed , (Thucydides), etc. 4. to be contrived, concocted , (Euripides), etc. 5. to be agreed on by two parties, (Thucydides): in participle agreed on, arranged , αἱ συγκείμεναι ἡμέραι (Herdotus Historicus); κατὰ τὰ συγκείμενα according to the terms agreed on , (Herdotus Historicus); ἐκ τῶν ξυγκειμένων (Thucydides) 6. impersonal σύγκειται, it has been or is agreed on , (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; so, συγκειμένου σφι, with infinitive, since they had agreed to . . , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

s: a regular collection of writings, a work, book, doctrine
6168.full: 1. that which is put together in order : 2. a body of troops, squadron, contingent , (Xenophon Historicus) 3. the constitution of a state , ς. πολιτείας a form of constitution, (Isocrates Orator) 4. an arrangement of musical notes , (Aristotle Philosopher) 5. a regular collection of writings, a work, book, doctrine , (Plutarch) 6. = σύνταξις II. 3, (Aeschines Orator) (ML)

6170.full: 1. to be controller of receipts and expenditure, to be treasurer, paymaster , (Aristophanes Comicus):—;with genitive, τ. τῆς Παράλου to be paymaster of the Paralus, (Demosthenes Orator) 2. at Rome, to be quaestor , (Plutarch) 3. transitive to deal out, dispense , (Plato Philosophus), etc.:—;Pass., τοὺς νόμους τεταμιεύμεθα we have the laws dealt out , (Lysias Orator):—;Mid., ταμιεύεσθαι εἰς ὅσον βουλόμεθα ἄρχειν to control the limits to which we mean to extend our sway, (Thucydides) 4. of keeping house, to regulate, manage , (Aristophanes Comicus):—; Pass., χώρα ταμιευομένα τινί governed or possessed by one, (Pindar) 5. to store up , (Demosthenes Orator); Ζηνὸς ταμιεύεσκε γονάς she was the depository of it, (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

6171.full: 1. troublous, turbulent , (Herdotus Historicus); ἴχνη τ. uncertain, baffling , (Xenophon Historicus) 2. troubled, disordered , (Aristotle Philosopher) 3. of an army, (Thucydides) 4. adverb, ταραχωδῶς ζῆν to live in a state of confusion , (Isocrates Orator); τ. ἔχειν πρός τινα to be rebelliously disposed, (Demosthenes Orator); Sup. -έστατα (Isocrates Orator) (ML)

s: buildings had been erected, there were buildings
6174.full: 1. to build a wall , (Aristophanes Comicus), etc.: with accusative cognate, τ. τεῖχος to build it, (Thucydides); so in Mid., τεῖχος ἐτειχίσσαντο they built them a wall, (Iliad by Homer):—;Pass. to be built , (Pindar): 3rd singular pluperfect τετείχιστο, impersonal, buildings had been erected, there were buildings , (Herdotus Historicus) 2. transitive to wall or fortify , τὸ οὖρος (Herdotus Historicus); τὴν πόλιν (Thucydides): in Mid., τειχίζεσθαι τὸ χωρίον (Thucydides):—;Pass. to be walled or fenced with walls , (Thucydides); τὰ τετειχισμένα the fortified parts , (Thucydides) (ML)

6175.full: 1. a broad strap for bearing anything from Root ! τλα, * τλάω, whence also the hero Telamon took his name, compare Ἄτλας 2. a leathern strap or belt , for bearing both shield or sword, (Homer) 3. a broad linen bandage for wounds, (Iliad by Homer); for swathing mummies, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

6179.full: 1. delightsome, delightful, pleasant, agreeable, glad , (Theognis Elegiacus), etc.; τὸ τερπνόν delight, pleasure , (Thucydides); τὰ τερπνά delights, pleasures , (Xenophon Historicus) 2. of persons, αὑτῷ τερπνός with joy to himself, (Sophocles Tragicus):—;comparative and Sup. τερπνότερος, -ότατος, (Theognis Elegiacus); later, -ιστος:—;adverb τερπνῶς, (Theognis Elegiacus) (ML)

s: so great, so noble, so bad
6182.full: antecedent to οἷος, as ἀοιδοῦ τοιοῦδ᾽ οἷος ὅδ᾽ ἐστί of such a minstrel as is this one, (Odyssey by Homer); absolute, ἀλλ᾽ ὅδ᾽ ἐγὼ τοιόσδε here am I such as you see , (Odyssey by Homer):—;also, so great, so noble, so bad , τοιάδε λαίφη such clothes, i. e. so bad , (Odyssey by Homer); τοσόσδε καὶ τοιόσδε (Herdotus Historicus):—;also with a qualifying word, τοιόσδ᾽ ἠμὲν δέμας ἠδὲ καὶ ἔργα such both in form and works, (Odyssey by Homer):—;with the Art., ὁ τ. ἀνήρ (Aeschulus Tragicus), etc.; οἱ τοιοίδε (Sophocles Tragicus); ἐν τῷ τοιῷδε in such circumstances, (Herdotus Historicus):—;the sense is made more indefinite in τοιόσδε τις such a one, (Thucydides):—;neuter plural τοιάδε as follows , τοιαῦτα as aforesaid , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

s: to the place from which it was cut
6183.full: 1. the end left after cutting, the stump of a tree, (Iliad by Homer); δοκοῦ τ. the end of a beam, (Thucydides); λίθοι ἐν τομῇ ἐγγώνιοι stones cut square, (Thucydides); so, τομῇ προσθεῖσα βόστρυχον having fitted the lock to the place from which it was cut , (Aeschulus Tragicus) 2. a cutting, hewing, cleaving , ἐν τομᾷ σιδήρου by stroke of iron, (Sophocles Tragicus); φασγάνου τομαί (Euripides):—;as a surgical operation, τομῇ χρῆσθαι (Plato Philosophus); διὰ καύσεών τε καὶ τομῶν by cautery and the knife , (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

6187.full: 1. on the third day , used with Verbs so as to agree with the subject, τριταῖοι ἐγένοντο ἐν τῇ Ἀττικῇ (Herdotus Historicus); ἐσβεβληκὼς τριταῖος ἐς Μηλιέας having invaded Melis three days before , (Herdotus Historicus); τρ. γενόμενος after being three days dead, (Herdotus Historicus):—; τριταῖος (i.e. πυρετός); a tertian fever , (Plato Philosophus) 2. of events, lasting three days , (Euripides) 3. generally for τρίτος, (Euripides) (ML)

6192.full: τρίχινος, -η, -ον (θρίξ), [in LXX: Zec.13:4 (שֵׂעָר), Exo.26:7 * ;] of hair: στόκος, Rev.6:12 (Xen., Plat., al.).† (AS)

6197.full: τάχα (ταχύς), adv., [in LXX: Wis.13:6 14:19 * ;] __(a) (chiefly poët.), quickly, presently; __(b) perhaps: Rom.5:7, Phm 15.† (AS)

6198.lxx: in LXX chiefly for מָהַר pi.
6198.full: τάχειον, see: ταχύ. ταχύ (neut. of ταχύς), adv., [in LXX chiefly for מָהַר pi. ;] quickly, speedily, forthwith: Mat.5:25 28:7-8, Mrk.9:39, Luk.15:22, Jhn.11:29, Rev.2:16 3:11 11:14 22:7, 12 22:2 o. Compar., τάχειον (T, Rec. τάχιον), = cl. θᾶσσον, θᾶττον (Att..), (see Bl., § 44, 3): Jhn.13:27 20:4, 1Ti.3:14 (T, Rec.), Heb.13:19, 23 Superl., τάχιστα: ὡς τ., as quickly as possible (BL, § 11, 3), Act.17:15.† (AS)
